description.narrative: (Tanzania): FY 2022 funds will support a new follow-on activity to the Landscape Conservation in Western Tanzania activity (TBD) that aims to reduce threats to chimpanzees and protect forest habitats in the Kigoma and Katavi regions. The follow-on activity will support regional and district authorities to develop and implement a strategic plan for conservation and support communities and local authorities to develop and implement inclusive land-use planning and district land-use frameworks that promote conservation and forest restoration in critical chimpanzee habitats outside of protected areas. .FY 2022 funds will also support management of the Gombe-Masito-Ugalla UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and provide technical assistance to districts developing management plans for two newly gazetted local authority forest reserves (Tongwe West and Masito). The primary threats to the biodiversity and remaining forest habitat in the western Tanzania landscape are the rapidly growing local population and its continued reliance on natural resources. With FY 2022 funds, USAID will strengthen local governance decision-making to scale successful land-use and natural resource management practices, promote sustainable livelihoods, engage with the private sector to support conservation-friendly agricultural value chains, and conduct social and behavior change interventions. .The LCWT activity also includes a reproductive health component that will support family planning services in four districts of the Kigoma and Katavi regions. ..This activity will contribute $1.5 million towards the Great Apes earmark of $1.5 million, $500,000 towards the Combating Wildlife Trafficking earmark of $3 million, and $737,500 towards the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises earmark of 3.5 million...
